To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nonparametric (and the wild bootstrap) are not consistent for the distribution of the cube root consistent maximum score estimator of a binary choice model, but that the bootstrap is consistent for the distribution when the criterion function is altered to be a function of the absolute values of the score.

1) the standard nonparameteric bootstrap for the maximum score estimator is inconsistent, 2) the nonparametric boostrap is consistent for the isotonic density estimators, 3) the standard nonparameteric bootstrap for the isotonic regression estimator is inconsistent, and 4) the nonparameteric boostrap is consistent when the isotonic regression is estimated with the least squares objective function.
the bootstrap-based distributional approximations for the maximum score estimator and the isotonic estimator can be made consistent by altering the shape function of the criterion function.
